question_text:
Cailan and Miles regularly play golf together, and have recorded their scores from their last 10 rounds:
Cailan: 84, 81, 86, 92, 85, 83, 80, 87, 90, 79
Miles: 87, 85, 83, 90, 88, 82, 84, 84, 91, 82

subparts.stem: Calculate the range and interquartile range for each data set.

mark_breakdown.desc: Finding maximum minus minimum for both players
Correct ranges for Cailan (13) and Miles (9)
Finding quartiles $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ for both players
Correct interquartile ranges for Cailan (6) and Miles (5)

subparts.solution:
Cailan:
$$\text{range} = \text{maximum} - \text{minimum} = 92 - 79 = 13$$
Lower half: 79, 80, 81, 83, 84 $\Rightarrow Q_1 = 81$
Upper half: 85, 86, 87, 90, 92 $\Rightarrow Q_3 = 87$
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 87 - 81 = 6$$

Miles:
$$\text{range} = \text{maximum} - \text{minimum} = 91 - 82 = 9$$
Lower half: 82, 82, 83, 84, 84 $\Rightarrow Q_1 = 83$
Upper half: 85, 87, 88, 90, 91 $\Rightarrow Q_3 = 88$
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 88 - 83 = 5$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Range is $\text{max} - \text{min}$. For an even number of values ($n=10$), split the ordered data evenly into halves of 5 values; $Q_1$ is the median of the lower half and $Q_3$ is the median of the upper half. $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
step_by_step: Find middle value of lower 5 values ($Q_1 = 81$) and upper 5 values ($Q_3 = 87$), so $\text{IQR} = 87 - 81 = 6$.
Find middle value of lower 5 values ($Q_1 = 83$) and upper 5 values ($Q_3 = 88$), so $\text{IQR} = 88 - 83 = 5$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Incorrectly splitting the dataset when computing quartiles.

subparts.stem: Which golfer had the lower: range

mark_breakdown.desc: Correctly identifying Miles' data as having the lower range

subparts.solution: Miles' data has the lower range ($9 < 13$).

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Compare the two calculated range values directly.
step_by_step: Cailan's range is 13; Miles' range is 9.
Since $9 < 13$, Miles has the lower range.

subparts.stem: Which golfer had the lower: interquartile range?

mark_breakdown.desc: Correctly identifying Miles' data as having the lower interquartile range

subparts.solution: Miles' data has the lower interquartile range ($5 < 6$).

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Compare the two calculated IQR values directly.
step_by_step: Cailan's IQR is 6; Miles' IQR is 5.
Since $5 < 6$, Miles has the lower IQR.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Mixing up the values of IQR between Cailan and Miles.

subparts.stem: Which measure of spread is more appropriate for determining who is generally the more consistent golfer? Explain your answer.
subparts.final_answer: $\text{The interquartile range, as it is less affected by outliers.}$

mark_breakdown.desc: Valid reason stating that the interquartile range is less affected by extreme values or outliers

subparts.solution: The interquartile range is more appropriate than the range for determining who is generally the more consistent golfer as it is less affected by outliers.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The interquartile range measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data and is resistant to extreme values (outliers), whereas range considers only the two extreme values.
step_by_step: Provide the justification: IQR is not distorted by extreme high or low scores (outliers).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Claiming that range is better because it uses all the extreme data.
